A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same work, and their shared text, tables, equations and figures are readable. However, v2 repeatedly references an appendix but ends after the references; v4 includes Supplement Materials. This limits comparison of the earlier method's exact supplementary details.

before.justification: v2 reports original MAE and SelectiveMAE experiments, including downstream classification, detection and segmentation scores, dataset-size studies and training-time measurements in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and reports additional dataset-scale results, memory measurements, component ablations and qualitative predictions in its main text and supplement.

M1.justification: Both describe HOG-guided partial reconstruction, cross-attention decoding and progressive semantic token selection, retaining the 85% masking and 25% reconstruction defaults. v4 specifies initialization, distance and staging rules, but v2's referenced appendix is unavailable. Whether these details merely specify or revise the exact earlier procedure cannot be established.

E1.justification: The six downstream benchmarks and their tasks remain unchanged. Compared with v2 Figure 2, v4 Figure 6 lists additional pre-training categories, including offshore platforms, radio towers, flagpoles, landfill and ski resorts. This is a limited coverage extension within the retained optical remote-sensing domain; the larger image count alone does not establish broader coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 5 retains the earlier downstream comparators and adds LSKNet-S and OREOLE with ViT-G. Figure 1 introduces an efficiency comparison including LocalMIM and several existing downstream baselines, while Table 7 evaluates AdaMAE's ATS selection strategy. These substantially broaden the alternatives compared for performance and efficiency.

E3.justification: v4 adds 8-million/100-epoch and 13-million/67-epoch MAE conditions, full-dataset SelectiveMAE runs, and memory evaluation on one A100 with batch size 256. Supplementary experiments vary reconstruction ratio, masking ratio, decoder depth and selection order; the reversed-order experiment also changes learning rate and batch size. These expand the evaluation design beyond newly disclosed settings.

E4.justification: v4 supplies reconstruction-strategy and component ablations in Tables 7–8, stability curves in Figure 4, feature-diversity analysis in Figure 2, and downstream prediction cases in Figures 8–11. These substantially strengthen analysis of design choices and behavior. The earlier extended-training study largely moves from v2 Table 2 to v4 Table 6.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the experimental scores. The additional tables and loss plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Earlier benchmark scores are retained, including the 4-million-image ViT-L DIOR/DIOR-R results of 77.80/70.31, now starred in v4 Table 5. A new 13-million-image row reports 78.70/71.75. v4 also adds larger-volume MAE results, memory measurements, comparator scores, ablations and qualitative outputs. Different pre-training volumes prevent interpreting the new scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Within the supplied material, v4 adds formal definitions of PSTS initialization sets and its stage-dependent min/max/random distance score in Equations 2–6. v2 provides a verbal account and the retained partial-reconstruction Equation 1. This expands mathematical specification without adding a theorem, proof or convergence guarantee.

C1.justification: The central dataset contribution expands from the claimed 4-million-image OpticalRS-4M resource to the 13-million-image OpticalRS-13M resource. v4's conclusion also adds GPU-memory savings to the efficiency claim. The pipeline contribution, 40% patch-use claim and greater-than-twofold training-speed claim remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of reconstruction, decoder-depth, masking and selection-order tradeoffs, including reasons for preferring HOG over ATS. Section 6.7 explicitly acknowledges underrepresentation of detection/segmentation data and remaining computational-access barriers. Earlier explanations involving foreground redundancy, complementary semantics and diminishing returns from longer training remain.

D1.justification: Section 6.4 and Table 9 newly document optimizers, learning rates, batches, warmups, augmentations, task-specific splits and software frameworks; the datasheet adds licensing and maintenance information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Conversely, v4 drops v2's direct project link, source-composition chart and explicit 300-epoch/last-200-epoch PSTS schedule, while asserting public availability without a direct dataset address.

R1.justification: The earlier cited works and overall positioning are retained. v4 adds AdaMAE, OREOLE-FM, LeMeViT, LSKNet, masked angle-aware autoencoding and the datasheets reference, with limited additional discussion of adaptive masking and geometric attributes. This updates the surrounding literature without substantially redefining the research position.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, condenses related-work and dataset-curation prose, simplifies the ablation-section hierarchy, and moves extended-training discussion into Section 6.2. Most of the introduction, methodological motivation and downstream narrative remains closely matched; the added scientific material does not amount to a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the predominantly single-column, red-highlighted presentation with a two-column layout, redraws the workflow and dataset displays, and relocates the category chart. It adds efficiency, stability, token-selection and prediction figures, plus ablation and configuration tables. The main comparison table also replaces publication metadata with parameter counts and changes result highlighting.

improvement.justification: Relative to the supplied v2, v4 substantially closes method-documentation and validation gaps: explicit PSTS definitions, Algorithm 1, Table 9 settings and Tables 7–8 ablations make the central approach much more assessable. Dataset transparency weakens through removal of the source chart and project link, and stale 4-million-image statements remain in the supplement. These defects temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial documentation and evidence gains.
